doc.title: Sherrie Maricle interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Cancelled festivals and rescheduling for DIVA and the trio
summary: DIVA's Brazil trip and the March Dizzy's recording were cancelled; she rebooked for March 2021, and the Gilmore and Berks festivals moved to 2021.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Yeah. With earplugs. Only kidding. But yeah, well this is just complete Twilight Zone time for all of us. Very crazy. And you know I will share, well today actually the DIVA Jazz Orchestra was scheduled to be in San Paolo, Brazil with Nneena Freelon, so we have had — one of the many festivals that were cancelled with all of my groups. So it’s painful and surreal to see all of those opportunities leave, and then, and with no end in sight for when we possibly will recoup even the smallest bit of live performance. It’s very strange.
Were any of the people that cancelled, did they try to do their best to say well we’re going to reschedule?

Yeah, in some cases I pursued it right away, like for example in March we were scheduled, usually DIVA does four nights at Dizzy’s Club in New York City, at Jazz at Lincoln Center every March, it’s our birthday and we’ve been playing there since the club opened. So we were scheduled in March to do a brand new live recording, “DIVA Swings Broadway” and it was cancelled, and I didn’t even fiddle around with trying to say well we’ll come in the fall. I just said please just put us down for next March, so we have our March 11 to the 14th everybody, 2021, DIVA Jazz. But the point of that is that any performing arts centers and even jazz clubs book at least a year in advance. So the majority of people booked through the end of this year and well into 2021. So it’ll be very hard to recoup everything. Another example, the Gilmore Keyboard Festival, which is a major piano festival in Kalamazoo Michigan, the trio was scheduled there. And that’s a massive multi-week event. It was cancelled, and hopefully we’ll be able to reschedule for 2021. Every opportunity is different. I know that the Berks Jazz Festival here in PA, the festival director John Onester just wrote to everybody and said, “Okay, everybody that was for 2020 we’re just going to do the same thing but in 2021. And that’s again, like dozens and dozens and dozens of acts over multiple days. So everyone is handling it differently.
